root_problem: The product-director standard chain needs a direct closed-loop pilot to prove each role handoff works without ambiguous inputs or noisy outputs.
business_goals: Deliver a small login and homepage experience through the full standard chain.
Collect direct evidence that product, design, implementation, review, QA, delivery, and user decision artifacts stay consumable by downstream gates.
acceptance_criteria: Anonymous users who request the homepage are redirected to the login page.
The login page exposes username and password fields.
A valid configured credential creates a session cookie and opens the homepage.
An invalid credential keeps the user on login with a readable error.
Logout clears the session and the old cookie cannot access the homepage.
design_decisions: Use a Python standard-library HTTP example app to avoid introducing an unrelated product stack.
Load login credentials from environment variables instead of hardcoding business secrets.
Use server-side session state with an HttpOnly SameSite=Lax cookie for the pilot journey.
non_functional_requirements: Exercise the feature through a real local HTTP server, not a mocked request object.
Keep implementation and test files below the repository 400-line file limit.
Keep the pilot isolated under examples/login_homepage_app and tests/test_login_homepage_app.py.
scope_boundaries: In scope: login form, credential validation, authenticated homepage, logout, and canonical chain evidence.
Out of scope: persistent users, browser CSS polish, production deployment, password reset, and multi-user administration.

delivery_plan.goal: ship and validate the login plus homepage pilot through a closed standard-chain run

director_confirmation.confirmation_basis: User delegated all standard-chain confirmations to Codex for the automated pilot.
